---
title: "Articles and how to cite them"
---

Every article on this site is listed below with its authors and a
reference that can be copied into a manuscript. The articles are web
pages without a DOI, so they are cited as web documents (APA 7th edition,
section 10.16): authors, year, title in italics, the site
name, and the address.

An article documents how a method is used; the method itself is
described in the package paper. When an analysis uses Nestimate, cite the
package paper, and cite an article in addition when the analysis follows
it:

> Saqr, M., López-Pernas, S., & Misiejuk, K. (2026). Nestimate: An R
> package for dynamic, probabilistic, and high order network analysis.
> *Applied Psychological Measurement*.
> https://doi.org/10.1177/01466216261472019

`citation("Nestimate")` prints the same reference in R, and
`toBibtex(citation("Nestimate"))` gives its BibTeX entry.

The articles are revised with the package. To point a reader to the text
you read, add the package version and the date you accessed it, for
example "(Nestimate 1.0.24; accessed 24 November 2026)".

## BibTeX

The same references for LaTeX and reference managers. Add a `note` field
with the version and access date.

```bibtex
@misc{nestimate_transition_networks,
  author       = {Saqr, Mohammed and L{\'o}pez-Pernas, Sonsoles and Misiejuk, Kamila},
  title        = {Network Estimation and Analysis with {Nestimate}},
  year         = {2026},
  url          = {https://pak.dynasite.org/Nestimate/articles/transition-networks.html}
}

@misc{nestimate_transition_entropy,
  author       = {Saqr, Mohammed},
  title        = {Transition Matrix Entropy},
  year         = {2026},
  url          = {https://pak.dynasite.org/Nestimate/articles/transition-entropy.html}
}

@misc{nestimate_markov_stability,
```
